doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

chapter: Vaudeville and the name Mac and Mac
title: Writing original material and what their act was
summary: Billy wrote all their material, which is why they could return often. Mary sang, danced and played leading lady; they did comedy songs together and whole acts.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Sure. I used to, in organizing these shows, I'd always sit down and write my material. And so we had, everything we had was original. That's why we could come back and also stay so long whenever we'd play any game. But we always had something new to offer. And I was the originator, see, with her help. And she could always sing. I never was a singer.
I was wondering, because on the record, you all both sang some. If your act is mostly a comedy act or singing, or just what did you do?

I sang. And we sang together. Comedy songs, you know. But I could dance a little. But I was leading lady, you know. Well, you look pretty and dance a little and sing. But we did our act. We had an act. Not an act. Acts.
Because when you go to New York, if you were doing vaudeville, when you go to New York...
